title: Preserve readable bounded column bands across generic single and bundle PDF exports
description: Users exporting wide authorized report definitions must receive every selected field in readable ordered column bands, with stable row identity and repeated section/header/provenance; this is shared export data preservation for all datasets, not a dedicated report or UI styling task. Stage 2 only. Keep legacy routes until every migration is genuinely accepted. No production, secrets/env, arbitrary SQL, permission expansion, new schema or unrelated refactor. Preserve concurrent work.
acceptance_criteria: Apply a reusable finite width and row-identity-aware horizontal column-band layout to both existing PDF exporters. All selected fields, field order and rows appear once per logical column band; repeat an authorized identity field when available, otherwise stable row ordinal. Never query hidden identity fields or drop/truncate columns; bounded pages and cancellation remain enforced.

Preserve independent section currency/unit, null versus zero, numeric formatting, summary/evidence coverage and nonempty/empty sections. Repeat readable headers at vertical page breaks, title and band/page provenance. Bound long cells without overlapping footer or silently clipping values; no cross-section arithmetic.

Test narrow and 27-plus-column multi-section inputs, long Chinese text, row continuity, numeric/null semantics, exact column coverage, cancellation and file limits. Run related tests and safe Release build/unit suite; generate real PDF and inspect rendered readability with actual artifacts before claiming layout acceptance.
implementation_evidence: ReportConfigurationBundlePdfExporter.cs ColumnWidths divides A4 usable width by all columns; real ERP-307 API .ai/logs/ERP-307-runtime-api-acceptance-20261005/bundle.pdf has 27-column sections and SO identifiers broken into 3-character lines. Generic exporters lack shared horizontal bands; all task history checked, no such shared capability.
